definitions.explanation: Small wooden or plastic blocks of various shapes that children stack and arrange to build structures. A classic children's toy.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{積|つ}み{木|き}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んでいる→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: The child is playing with building blocks.

examples.japanese: {積|つ}み{木|き}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{高|たか}く→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{積|つ}み{上|あ}げて→積み上げる：07920_tsumiageru⟧⟦{塔|とう}→塔：09944_tou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I stacked the blocks high and built a tower.

examples.japanese: ⟦カラフル→カラフル：10803_karafuru⟧な{積|つ}み{木|き}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{想像力|そうぞうりょく}→想像力：17615_souzouryoku⟧や⟦{手先|てさき}→手先：12939_tesaki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{器用|きよう}→器用：02655_kiyou⟧さ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{育|そだ}てる→育てる：01235_sodateru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{役立|やくだ}つ→役立つ：03168_yakudatsu⟧。
examples.english: Colorful building blocks are useful for developing children's imagination and manual dexterity.

notes:
USAGE:
{積|つ}み{木|き} typically refers to traditional wooden blocks, though modern versions come in various materials. It is one of the most common and recognizable children's toys in Japan.
Sometimes used figuratively to describe something built up carefully that can be easily toppled, similar to "house of cards" in English.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {積|つ}み{木|き}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧ (to play with blocks)
- {積|つ}み{木|き}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{積|つ}む→積む：02294_tsumu⟧ (to stack blocks)
- {積|つ}み{木|き}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{崩|くず}す→崩す：03919_kuzusu⟧ (to knock down blocks)
- ⟦{木製|もくせい}→木製：13083_mokusei_b⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{積|つ}み{木|き} (wooden blocks)
